Wrote lit.md for seed 805 round 3 (C group, literature-officer role), addressing analysis.md's four literature questions: L1 rolling skewness/kurtosis/extremes vs rolling mean of daily characteristics (MAX effect, realized skewness/kurtosis, trend factor, momentum/52-week-high "echo" effect and its skip-period fix, attention proxies); L2 volume slow-growth and opening/closing call-auction volume share, normalization methods, and separation from liquidity level/market cap (GKM's window-rank normalization read directly from the working paper, Lee-Swaminathan volume trend, Bogousslavsky-Muravyev's auction-share-as-signal, two China-specific Shanghai closing-auction studies pinning the 2018-08-20 regime break); L3 whether minute-return kurtosis is the same thing as zero-return-ratio/illiquidity (Lesmond-Ogden-Trzcinka, Bekaert-Harvey-Lundblad, and a directly-read 2020 FRL paper regressing kurtosis on five liquidity proxies including zero-return days, plus a China price-limit-hit mechanics paper); L4 intraday price-volume correlation (CPV) aggregation methods and direction (Gallant-Rossi-Tauchen, Chan-Fong, a China sell-side RPV factor report flagged as lower-confidence, and Llorente et al. reused for a different point than r2). Three papers (Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw, Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin, Wang-Hudson-Rhodes-Zhang-Gregoriou) were verified by downloading the PDF and reading the methodology/results text directly with pdftotext rather than relying on search summaries. Only pre-2023-08-08 sources were used; every claim is tagged to a 19-row source table with title/authors/year-month/venue/link/verified flag/notes, and several "searched, found nothing" gaps are reported honestly rather than filled in.
